brief.summary: Note first: I have no hydrodynamics or baryonic emulator tool. My only tools were arXiv and web search, so I did not compute any z=0 Pk-ratio (P_hydro/P_DMO) values. Any numbers for specific parameter points have to come from running BACCO (2011.15018), BCemu (2108.08863), HMcode-2020 (2009.01858) or the van Daalen et al. power-spectrum library (1906.00968) locally. I give no suppression amplitudes because I did not read results beyond titles and short abstracts. Physics: AGN feedback, and stellar feedback in lower-mass haloes, pushes gas out of group- and cluster-mass haloes (about 1e13-1e14.5 Msun). This lowers their baryon fraction and flattens their inner mass profiles, which suppresses P(k) at k of about 0.1-10 h/Mpc relative to dark-matter-only runs. At higher k, gas cooling and star formation push the ratio back up. Several groups (van Daalen 1906.00968, resummation model 2509.04552, Debackere 1908.05765, BAHAMAS/cosmo-OWLS 2309.06479, TNG 2511.10634) find the suppression is mainly set by the baryon fraction of group-scale haloes. That ties it to X-ray, tSZ and kSZ observables. For weak lensing, these scale-dependent changes bias S8 if left out (1105.1075, 1407.4301). Amon and Efstathiou (2206.11794, 2305.09827) argue that stronger-than-standard nonlinear suppression could reconcile KiDS and DES cosmic shear with Planck, and recent kSZ/X-ray results (FLAMINGO 2410.17109, 2602.02484) hint that feedback may be stronger than in fiducial simulations. Current mitigation options are scale cuts, marginalising over HMcode or baryonification parameters, theory-error covariances (2410.12500), and outside constraints from SZ, X-ray or FRBs (2301.02186, 2401.03510, 2501.17922).

result.summary:
I ran three HACC Pk-ratio (P_hydro/P_grav) predictions at z=0 with cosmology held fixed (omega_m=0.14, sigma_8=0.8, kappa_w=3, M_seed=1.3). Two success criteria are not fully met: values at k=5-10 h/Mpc and the location and depth of the suppression minimum were not extracted. The text reader cuts each 799-bin CSV off near k=3.7 h/Mpc, and load_table_data rejects the CSV header row (posted as q-06). The fiducial point is the centre of the parameter ranges, not a calibrated fiducial.

Parameter points:
- fiducial_z0: e_w=0.6, v_kin=0.65, eps_kin=0.61
- strongAGN_z0: e_w=1.0, v_kin=1.2, eps_kin=1.2
- weakAGN_z0: e_w=0.2, v_kin=0.1, eps_kin=0.02

Ratio at k=0.10 / 0.51 / 1.00 / 2.00 / 3.0 / 3.71 h/Mpc:
- Fiducial: 0.99968 / 0.99197 / 0.97832+/-0.00096 / 0.95104+/-0.00229 / 0.91968 / 0.8979
- Strong: 0.99962 / 0.99062 / 0.97506+/-0.00175 / 0.94463+/-0.00405 / 0.91207 / 0.8904
- Weak: 1.00009 / 1.00096 / 1.0023+/-0.0025 / 1.0089 / 1.0074 / 1.0012+/-0.0105. This is an enhancement, peaking at about 1.0097 near k=2.4 h/Mpc.

For the fiducial and strong points the suppression is still deepening at k=3.7 h/Mpc, so their minimum lies above k=3.7 h/Mpc.

Comparison at k=1 h/Mpc: suppression is 2.2% (fiducial), 2.5% (strong) and -0.2% (weak). All three agree with HSC-XXL (5+/-4%) within about 1.4 sigma. None reaches eROSITA+kSZ (10+/-2%, 2512.02954); the strong point falls short by about 3.7 sigma. Pushing e_w, v_kin and eps_kin together to their upper limits changes the k=1 suppression by only about 0.3 percentage points relative to the fiducial. The emulator 1-sigma at k=1 (0.1-0.25%) is comparable to that fiducial-to-strong difference but well below the weak-to-fiducial difference (2.4%).

result.summary:
This direction is only partly done. The literature synthesis is posted as finding f-003 and rests on the abstracts and introductions of five full texts. These are saved under /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-combo-baryonic-pk/runs/261017_143153/ as 2410.17109.txt, 2512.02954.txt, 2309.07959.txt, 2206.11794.txt and 2309.02920.txt.

Mechanism, from those texts:
- Energy injected by AGN moves gas relative to the dark matter and suppresses small-scale power by tens of percent compared with dark-matter-only runs (2512.02954).
- Below about 10 Mpc, AGN push baryons outward, while on smaller scales star formation concentrates baryons in halo centres (2309.02920).
- In FLAMINGO (2410.17109), the response is stronger for lower group and cluster gas fractions, for collimated jets instead of thermal winds, and for lower stellar mass at fixed gas fraction.
- As redshift falls, the FLAMINGO response grows and its minimum moves to smaller scales. The dependence on cosmology is about 1 percent at k<10 h/Mpc. Its emulator is accurate to better than 1 percent up to k=10 h/Mpc and z=3.

Benchmarks at k=1 h/Mpc:
- eROSITA plus kSZ: 10 +/- 2 percent; HSC-XXL: 5 +/- 4 percent. Both are for haloes with 13<log10 M500<14 at 0<z<1 (2512.02954).
- Cluster-based baryon-correction priors (2309.02920): 0.042 (+0.012/-0.014) at k=1 h/Mpc and 0.184 (+0.026/-0.031) at k=3 h/Mpc. The effect is below 1 percent for k<0.37 h/Mpc at 97.5 percent credibility.

Weak lensing:
- KiDS-1000 shear gives S8 = 0.759 (+0.024/-0.021). This can be reconciled with Planck LCDM if nonlinear power is suppressed more strongly than simulations predict (2206.11794).
- FLAMINGO concludes that baryon physics is unlikely to be driving the S8 tension (2309.07959).
- The mitigation route demonstrated for LSST Y1 is to calibrate feedback models with multi-wavelength gas observables (2512.02954).

Citations: 2410.17109, 2309.07959 and 2206.11794 were cited with verbatim quotes into references.bib in the run directory.

findings.claim: Literature synthesis from full texts that were read: (1) Mechanism: energy from active galactic nuclei (AGN) moves gas relative to the dark matter. This suppresses the nonlinear matter power by tens of percent compared with dark-matter-only runs (2512.02954). Below about 10 Mpc, AGN redistribute baryons outward, while on smaller scales star formation concentrates baryons in halo centres (2309.02920). In FLAMINGO, lower group and cluster gas fractions, collimated jets instead of thermal winds, and lower stellar mass at fixed gas fraction all strengthen the response. As z falls, the response grows and its minimum moves to smaller scales. The cosmology dependence is about 1 percent at k<10 h/Mpc (2410.17109). (2) Benchmarks: suppression at k=1 h/Mpc is 10+/-2 percent from eROSITA plus kSZ and 5+/-4 percent from HSC-XXL, over 13<log10 M500/(Msun/h)<14 and 0<z<1 (2512.02954). Cluster baryon-correction-model priors give 0.042 (+0.012/-0.014) at k=1 h/Mpc and 0.184 (+0.026/-0.031) at k=3 h/Mpc, with less than 1 percent impact at k<0.37 h/Mpc at 97.5 percent credibility (2309.02920). (3) Weak lensing: Amon and Efstathiou find that KiDS-1000 (S8 = 0.759 +0.024/-0.021) can be reconciled with Planck LCDM if nonlinear power is suppressed more strongly than simulations predict (2206.11794). FLAMINGO finds baryonic effects are not large enough to remove the S8 tension (2309.07959). Mitigation is to calibrate feedback with multi-wavelength gas observables (2512.02954).

questions.text: Does the HACC emulator's Pk-ratio k range reach 10 h/Mpc and beyond, so that the suppression minimum and the upturn at higher k are actually covered? If the range is truncated, the report must state it.
Which emulator parameters map most directly onto AGN feedback strength, and do their ranges span suppression levels comparable to both the HSC-XXL and the eROSITA plus kSZ constraints at k=1 h/Mpc?
The S8 impact will come from the literature rather than our own shear forecast, because no tool computes C_ell or xi_plus. Should a projected-lensing estimate be flagged as future work?
Are the emulator's uncertainties at z=0 small compared with the differences between feedback variants, so that the conclusions are meaningful?

issues.text: Every literature-comparison significance on the board (f-024, f-029, f-036) depends on f-020 and f-021, and neither has been checked verbatim. The full texts are already on disk, so checking them is cheap. Until it is done, the headline conclusion that HACC falls short of eROSITA+kSZ by about 3 sigma is provisional.

The emulator values for lowM are supported. The comparisons to Siegel et al. and Grandis et al. inherit the contested status of f-020 and f-021. The claim that 'the design range does not reach eROSITA+kSZ' has only been tested at the kappa_w=2, e_w=1 corners with omega_m=0.14 and sigma_8=0.8. The lowM curve is still falling at k=3.7, so its minimum is unresolved. The cosmology axes (omega_m 0.12-0.155, sigma_8 0.7-0.9) were not explored, and they can shift the response through the baryon fraction and halo abundance.

There is a physically interesting signal here that the finding does not develop. Strong kinetic feedback leaves f_gas(<R500c) at 1.26e14 essentially unchanged (0.1214 vs 0.1221), yet it deepens S(k). That suggests the HACC suppression is driven by gas removal beyond R500c, or by other halo masses, rather than by the R500c gas fraction. A controlled single-parameter sweep is needed to test this.

Attributing the deeper suppression to 'kappa_w=2 vs kappa_w=3' is confounded, because M_seed also differs (2.0 vs 1.3). Note too that f-036 shows lower M_seed increases suppression. That makes the kappa_w attribution plausible, but it has not been isolated by changing one parameter at a time.

The weak-lensing assessment is still qualitative. There is no Delta S8 value (Table 4 of 2410.12500 is unread), the HACC k=0.2-0.3 values are interpolated rather than read, and there is no A_mod-equivalent number for any HACC point. Two directions in a row hit their budget limit before reading the files they had produced. Future reads should target narrow character ranges.
